resources.string: Stand near the car with Bluetooth on. The app finds the box, pairs with it and remembers its key on this phone, encrypted.
Not connected to the box yet
%1$s: sent, no confirmation from the box
Connects when the app is open
Turn it on to reach the car
The app needs it to find and connect to the box
Short scan to find its address
Connects by itself when you get close
Paired: a new key was set and saved on this phone.
Asking the box who it is
New box: pairing a new key
The box is paired with a key this phone doesn\'t have
The box refused the stored key
The box refused the new key
The device at this address doesn\'t speak the box\'s protocol
Not in range, or connected to another phone
The box didn\'t answer as expected
Stand near the car. Boxes in range appear below; pick yours and give it a name.
If the box is already paired (for example with the original app) and you know its 16-byte key, add it with the key and the app reuses the pairing.
Connect to the box to see and change this.
%1$s and its key will be deleted from this phone. The box keeps its key: to use it again you will need the key, or reset the box.
Then hold the card to the reader for 10 seconds
Hold the card to the reader now…
Pair again with a new key
Removes the current key from the box and sets a new one
The box forgets its current key: every other phone or app using it stops working. A new random key is set and saved here.
Raw vendor settings (what lock, unlock and remote start also do, car model). The original app downloads them from its server; only send values you know are right for your car.
Send %1$d bytes to the box? Wrong values can change how the car reacts.
Paired automatically on the first connection, or import a key
Copied, cleared from the clipboard in a minute
A key is %1$d bytes: %2$d hex digits
The key is stored encrypted on this phone. Keep exported copies somewhere safe: whoever has the key can open the car.
The previous key is kept as a backup.

The box decides, measuring this phone: the phone must stay connected all the time (Stay connected), which uses more battery. Smart unlock does the same from the phone, connecting only when Android sees the car nearby. Only one of the two can be on.
Smart unlock is on: turning this on turns smart unlock off.
Comfort entry (legacy) and smart unlock can\'t be on together: smart unlock will be turned off.

Unlocks the car when you get close and locks it when you walk away, with the app closed. Android notices the car nearby with almost no battery; only then does the phone connect and measure the signal.
On: waiting for the car to be in range
Unlocked: locks when you walk away
Done for this visit: active again once you have left
Locked: unlocks again if you come back soon
If you come back after locking
After locking, the car unlocks again if you come back within this time (you forgot something), even without leaving the Bluetooth range. Then it rests until you have left.
%1$s locked: unlocks again if you come back within %2$d min
Suspended (you passed by the car several times). Resumes by itself at %1$s
A short double vibration and a quiet notification when the car locks by itself; a long one if it couldn\'t be locked.
Smart unlock couldn\'t lock the car as you walked away
Confirms that smart unlock locked the car as you walked away

The phone measures the signal where you open the car and where it should lock, and proposes the distances. Carry the phone as you usually do (pocket, bag). Meanwhile smart unlock doesn\'t open or lock the car.
Where you want the car to open. Stay still while it measures.
Now walk to where it should lock
A few metres away: where you usually are when you turn to look at the car. Stay still while it measures.
No signal reading: stay in range of the car and try again
The two spots read almost the same signal: measure the second one further from the car, or it may open and lock too easily.
Notifications are off for this app: you wouldn\'t be told if the car may have been left unlocked.
Paused by you: nothing opens or locks the car by itself until you resume
Nothing opens or locks the car by itself until you resume. The car was left as it was.
This box can\'t unlock and lock on its own commands.
Connect to the box to turn it on: Android asks once to pair it as a companion device.
Couldn\'t turn smart unlock on, see the log
The car wasn\'t paired as a companion device
Comfort entry (legacy) is on in the box. The two can\'t be on together: it will be turned off.
Signal as this phone measures it: the lower the number, the closer to the car.

Unlocking needs you close to the car (never beyond -75 dBm, a few metres). Locking happens while you walk away and the phone is still connected (never beyond -88 dBm): with no signal left, the car can\'t be locked.
The box changed its Bluetooth address, so Android no longer recognises it. Turn smart unlock on again near the car.
The connection dropped before the car could be locked (you walked away fast, or the signal was lost). Check the car, or lock it from the app when you are near.
Live signal, read every second while this screen is open: move the sliders to where you stand
The live signal appears here when the car is in range.
Unlocks only if the phone isn\'t on its lock screen: protects against signal relay attacks, but you have to take the phone out.

If you only pass by the car, the next time you need to come closer; after a few pass-bys in a short time smart unlock suspends itself (a notification lets you resume it, or it resumes on its own after a few hours).
Smart unlock: the phone decides and connects only near the car. Legacy: the box decides and the phone stays connected all the time. Only one can be on.
Built into the box: it measures the phone\'s signal and opens or locks by itself, as long as the phone stays connected
Comfort entry (legacy) is on in the box
The box itself still opens and locks by distance. It can\'t run together with smart unlock: turn it off here, or turning smart unlock on will do it.
Near %1$s: unlocks when you get close
%1$s unlocked: locks when you walk away
Near %1$s: unlock the phone to open the car
Shown only while the car is in range
You passed by the car several times in a short time, so it isn\'t unlocked and locked automatically for now. Tap Resume to turn it back on, or it resumes by itself in a few hours.
The box unlocks when you come close and locks when you walk away, measuring this phone\'s signal. It only works while the phone stays connected.
Comfort entry is on, but the phone disconnects when the app closes: turn on Stay connected.
Reading the settings from the box…
Done by the box while connected
Signal strength: the lower the number, the closer to the car.
Reads the signal every 1.5 s while this screen is open
Keeps the link with the app closed (needed by comfort entry). Uses more battery.
Smart unlock turned off: with the link always up, Android can\'t see the car come and go.
The app measures this phone\'s signal at two places: where the car should unlock and where it should lock. Each takes 30 seconds.
Stand where you want the car to unlock, with the phone where you usually carry it, then start.
Go to where the car should lock (a few metres away), then start.
These thresholds come from your measurements. Apply them to turn comfort entry on.
Choose the buttons on the home screen and their order. Tap the line under a button to switch between single tap and press-and-hold.
The box\'s own command for this action: try this first.

One tap in the app: the box presses the remote\'s button for you, as many times and as long as set here. For cars that open the trunk with a long press or a double click, or lower the windows by holding unlock.
A safety for actions you don\'t want to trigger by mistake
Android requires it while staying connected; you can hide it here
Every connection step and command, for diagnosis
Shown while the app stays connected to the car
